title: Aspect Deep 9: Mixed Review (All Eight Contexts)
description: Synthesis. Mixes negation, frequency, completion, imperatives, phase verbs, modal verbs, the conditional, and narrative sequencing.
descriptionRussian: Итоговый урок. Смешивает все темы трека: отрицание, частотность, завершение, повелительное наклонение, фазовые и модальные глаголы, условное наклонение и последовательность в рассказе.
intro: Eight contexts, one underlying question. Process or completion, repeated or single, ongoing or bounded: every lesson here asked that in a different frame. Some frames allow only one answer and some leave the choice to you. Today they arrive mixed, and part of the work is noticing which kind you are in.
rules: Each B1 aspect context applies the same underlying logic: process versus completion, single event versus repeated activity, ongoing background versus bounded foreground.
The trigger and the context change; the aspect rules do not. Identify the family or context first; then apply the matching rule.

Some contexts allow only one aspect (phase verbs → impf; pf imperative for specific request; pf in chained narrative storyline). Others allow both, with one as the default and the other as the marked choice (modal verbs default to impf; не + verb defaults to impf for prohibition).
When two contexts cooperate in one sentence (e.g., conditional + completion adverb, or background impf + foreground pf), each verb is decided independently.
examples: Я не читал эту книгу. (Не + impf: no engagement. L1.)
Маша редко пила кофе по утрам. (Frequency cues stacked → impf. L2.)
Антон вдруг понял ошибку. (Suddenness → pf. L3.)
Не разбей вазу! (Negative pf imperative as warning. L4.)
Они продолжают учить русский. (Phase verb + impf inf. L5.)
Я хочу прочитать эту книгу к выходным. (Modal + bounded plan → pf inf. L6.)
Если бы я знал её адрес, я бы написал ей. (Conditional: impf-only verb stays impf, pf single event in result. L7.)
Я пил кофе, когда позвонил Антон. (Background impf + foreground pf. L8.)

rows.label: Negation
cells: Не + impf = no engagement; не + pf = didn't finish
Я не читал / Я не прочитал.

rows.label: Imperative
cells: Pf specific / impf habit; не impf prohibition / не pf warning

rows.label: Modal verbs
cells: + Impf default; pf for specific bounded plan

rows.label: Conditional
cells: Если бы я знал, я бы сказал.

rows.label: Narrative
cells: Pf chain for storyline; impf for background
Я пил кофе, когда позвонил Антон.

items.prompt: Я _____ домой, открыл дверь и увидел гостей.
items.promptEnglish: I (m) came home, opened the door, and saw the guests.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 8: three sequenced storyline events. Aspect?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 8: a chain of sequenced storyline events takes chained perfectives. Past masc -ёл: пришёл. The other two verbs (открыл, увидел) match. Today's lesson synthesizes all eight B1 aspect contexts.

items.promptEnglish: Don't drink cold water; you'll get sick!
items.hint: Standard prohibition. Lesson 4: which negative imperative aspect?
items.explanation: A standard 'don't do this' prohibition uses не + imperfective imperative: не пей. The perfective не выпей would be a warning against accidentally drinking it all in one go, which the long-term illness reasoning does not target.

items.prompt: Маша начала _____ длинный роман на этой неделе.
items.promptEnglish: Masha started reading a long novel this week.
items.hint: Lesson 5: phase verbs take which infinitive?
items.explanation: Phase verbs take ONLY an imperfective infinitive. Начала + читать. The perfective прочитать is ungrammatical after a phase verb, regardless of whether the eventual reading would be 'completed.'

items.prompt: Если бы Антон _____ книгу до конца, он бы понял мою точку зрения.
items.promptEnglish: If Anton had read the book through to the end, he would have understood my point of view.
items.hint: Lesson 7: conditional plus completion phrase 'до конца.' Aspect?
items.explanation: 'До конца' is a completion phrase that locks in the perfective. The conditional does not change this rule. Past masc -л + бы: прочитал. The imperfective читал would describe a hypothetical reading-process without completion, which the result-clause depends on.

items.promptEnglish: I love reading books on weekends.
items.hint: Lesson 6: любить + general preference + habitual cue. Aspect?
items.explanation: Любить is a verb of general preference and takes an imperfective infinitive. The habitual cue 'по выходным' (Lesson 2) reinforces. Любить + читать. The perfective прочитать would describe a single completed reading, which 'love reading' on weekends cannot pair with.

items.prompt: По выходным мы _____ старые фильмы у бабушки.
items.promptEnglish: On weekends we watched old films at Grandma's.
items.hint: Lesson 2: 'по выходным' is which kind of cue?
items.explanation: 'По выходным' is a по + dative plural habitual time pattern (Lesson 2) and triggers the imperfective. Past plural -ли: смотрели. The perfective посмотрели would mark a single completed viewing, which the every-weekend frame rules out.

items.promptEnglish: Anton finally read the article through.
items.hint: The completion adverb forces which aspect?
items.explanation: Наконец-то ('finally') marks a reached result, which takes the perfective past: прочитал статью. Читал would describe an open-ended process, clashing with the completion adverb.

items.promptEnglish: On weekends I watched this film.
items.hint: По выходным is a habitual cue.
items.explanation: The habit cue по выходным takes the imperfective past: смотрел. Посмотрел frames one completed viewing.

items.hint: Phase verbs take only which infinitive?
items.explanation: Phase verbs like начать take only an imperfective infinitive: начала читать. Прочитать cannot follow a phase verb.

items.promptEnglish: Don't break the vase - it's very expensive!
items.hint: A warning against one accidental act.
items.explanation: A warning against an unintended single act takes не + perfective: Не разбей вазу. Не разбивай would be a general prohibition ('make a habit of not breaking things'), the wrong frame for one risky moment.

items.prompt: Я хочу _____ эту книгу к выходным.
items.promptEnglish: I want to read this book through by the weekend.
items.hint: A bounded plan with a deadline after хотеть.
items.explanation: The deadline ('к выходным') makes the plan bounded, so the perfective infinitive: хочу прочитать. Читать would name only the process.

items.promptEnglish: I have never read this book.
items.hint: Никогда + не denies the action ever happened.
items.explanation: Total denial across time takes не + imperfective: никогда не читал. Не прочитал would only deny finishing on one occasion; the никогда frame wants the imperfective.

blanks: Маша часто _____ кофе по утрам. (Masha often drank coffee in the mornings.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Two stacked frequency cues: часто (Lesson 2) and по утрам (Lesson 2). Both → imperfective. Past fem -ла: пила. The perfective выпила would mark a single completed drinking, which 'часто' and 'по утрам' both rule out.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я ни разу не прочитал эту книгу, хотя купил её давно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have not read this book even once, although I bought it long ago.
errorCorrection.explanation: Under negation, 'ни разу' (not once) pairs with the imperfective for the 'no engagement on any occasion' reading: ни разу не читал (Lesson 1). The perfective прочитал would specifically deny finishing on a single occasion, which is narrower than 'never even started'. The rule: не + imperfective denies that the action took place; не + perfective denies its completion.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша долго искала ключи и наконец находила их в сумке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha looked for the keys for a long time and finally found them in her bag.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Наконец' (finally) is an emphatic completion adverb and triggers the perfective: нашла (Lesson 3). The long search 'долго искала' is the imperfective process; the moment of finding is the single completed result. The imperfective находила would describe finding as a repeated or ongoing process ('kept finding'), which 'finally' contradicts.

errorCorrection.sentence: После ужина гости продолжали поговорить на кухне.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: After dinner, the guests kept chatting in the kitchen.
errorCorrection.explanation: Продолжать is a phase verb of continuation and takes only an imperfective infinitive: продолжали разговаривать (Lesson 5). The perfective поговорить ('have a brief, bounded chat') claims a contained result, which contradicts the open-ended 'keep doing' meaning of a continuation verb. Phase verbs admit no perfective infinitive.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) have never drunk this wine.
minimalPairs.explanation: Lesson 1 / Lesson 2: никогда (never) under не pairs with the imperfective for the 'no engagement, ever' reading. Past masc -л: пил. The perfective выпил would specifically deny a single completed drink, which is narrower than 'never tried it.'

Lesson 3: наконец-то is an emphatic completion adverb and triggers the perfective. Past fem -ла: написала. The imperfective писала would describe an ongoing writing process, which 'finally finished' contradicts.

patternRecognition.sentence: Маша редко пила кофе по утрам.
patternRecognition.question: What triggers the imperfective in this sentence?
patternRecognition.explanation: Two stacked frequency cues: редко and по утрам. Both → imperfective. Past fem -ла: пила. This is the Lesson 2 family at work.

patternRecognition.question: What forces the imperfective infinitive here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Начать is a phase verb of beginning. Phase verbs take ONLY an imperfective infinitive. Начал + читать. This is the sharpest rule in the track: there is no perfective option after a phase verb.

patternRecognition.question: Why is this imperative perfective?
patternRecognition.explanation: The speaker is not forbidding the listener from breaking vases in general; they are warning against the specific accident with this expensive vase. Не + perfective imperative: не разбей. The standard prohibition (impf) would be 'Не разбивай вазы.'

patternRecognition.sentence: Я пил кофе, когда позвонил Антон.
patternRecognition.question: Why does this sentence mix the two aspects?
patternRecognition.explanation: The drinking was already in progress when the call interrupted. Background ongoing → impf пил. Foreground single event → pf позвонил. The two aspects do different jobs in the same sentence: impf sets the scene, pf marks the event.

reviewVocab.definition: phase verb (a verb that marks the beginning, continuation, or end of an action; takes only an imperfective infinitive)
reviewVocab.example: Фазовые глаголы (начать, продолжать, закончить) сочетаются только с инфинитивом НСВ.

reviewVocab.definition: the conditional mood (built from past-tense forms with бы; aspect choice follows past-tense rules)
reviewVocab.example: В условном наклонении вид выбирается по тем же правилам, что и в обычном прошедшем.

reviewVocab.definition: background (an action already in progress when something else happened; takes the imperfective in narrative)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я пил кофе, когда позвонил Антон' слово 'пил' создаёт фон.
